title: Image Compression Using Quantum Wavelet Transform and Quantum Convolutional Networks
authors: Harshdeep Jadhav, Sreeraj Rajan Warrier, Jayasri Dontabhaktuni
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid quantum-classical framework for grayscale image compression and decompression, leveraging the strengths of quantum computing and deep learning. The compression pipeline integrates a Variational Quantum Daubechies Wavelet Transform (V-QDWT) and a trainable Quantum Convolutional Neural Network (QCNN) optimized end-to-end to achieve efficient, image-adaptive multi-resolution analysis and entanglement-based feature reduction. Input images are encoded using the Normal Arbitrary Superposition State (NASS) representation, enabling compact and scalable quantum storage. For decompression, we implement inverse QCNN and V-QDWT circuits to reconstruct coarse image features natively, followed by a classical Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) to enhance perceptual quality. Experimental evaluations on benchmark grayscale datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our hybrid approach. By jointly training the quantum layers, the base quantum pipeline closely rivals classical JPEG2000 standards. Subsequent SRGAN refinement substantially pushes the boundaries of the reconstruction, achieving superior structural fidelity (PSNR: 30.0667 dB, SSIM: 0.8744, Histogram Correlation: 0.9244). Histogram analysis and qualitative comparisons further validate the restoration of fine textures and intensity distributions. Our findings highlight the potential of combining variational quantum compression with classical deep learning to enable efficient, scalable, and perceptually-aware image processing in quantum-enhanced computing environments.
summary: This work proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework for image compression, combining Variational Quantum Wavelet Transforms and Quantum CNNs for quantum feature extraction. The quantum latent representation is then refined using a classical Super-Resolution GAN, achieving state-of-the-art perceptual quality metrics. It demonstrates the potential of quantum computation to enhance classical signal processing tasks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficient and high-fidelity image compression and decompression by integrating quantum computational techniques with classical deep learning models.
main_result: The hybrid quantum-classical framework achieves superior structural fidelity, with the final reconstruction significantly surpassing baseline quantum methods by incorporating a classical Super-Resolution GAN.
method: The process involves encoding images into quantum states (NASS), performing multi-resolution analysis using a Variational Quantum Daubechies Wavelet Transform (V-QDWT), and feature reduction via a trainable Quantum Convolutional Neural Network (QCNN).
model_or_system: The core model is a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline tested on NISQ hardware (IBM Fez) and simulated. It utilizes quantum circuits for state preparation, wavelet transforms, and convolutional layers, followed by classical SRGAN refinement.
key_observables: PSNR (30.0667 dB), SSIM (0.8744), and Histogram Correlation (0.9244) are key performance metrics used to validate reconstruction quality.
important_parameters: The compression ratio is mathematically defined (e.g., 4:1), and the process involves mapping pixel intensities to quantum rotation angles ($\phi_i$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the feasibility of implementing inverse QCNN and QDWT circuits, and that classical SRGAN post-processing is necessary to restore perceptual quality lost during quantum compression.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overall hybrid framework schematic, quantum circuits for NASS state preparation and wavelet transforms, and comparisons showing the improvement from base quantum reconstruction to SRGAN-refined output.
paper_structure: The paper details the encoding (NASS), the quantum compression pipeline (V-QDWT $ightarrow$ QCNN), the decompression pipeline (Inverse QCNN $ightarrow$ IQDWT $ightarrow$ SRGAN), and includes ablation studies comparing quantum vs. classical components.
why_interesting: While focused on image processing, the reliance on variational quantum circuits (V-QDWT, QCNN) for feature extraction and dimensionality reduction provides a concrete, near-term application of quantum machine learning algorithms.
